name: Hanzi Quest
pitch: A practice notebook for reading Chinese, taught in an order where each character makes the next easier.
problem: Learning to read Chinese can feel like memorising pictures.

stats.label: characters in 12 stages, plus a kitchen pack
skills kept apart: read, say, recall, write
radicals taught, each with its characters

features.title: Characters in families
features.text: Most characters are two parts: one hints at the meaning, one at the sound.
details: Learn a radical once and every character carrying it gets easier
Each card names its parts: 大 big + 人 person
A Words you can read deck fills itself as characters pile up

screen.alt: The radicals page explaining 女 woman plus 马 mǎ makes 妈 mā, mum

features.title: Read a real menu
features.text: One character a day from a restaurant menu, inked in as you learn it.
details: The menu grows with you: dishes, then descriptions, then specials
Hover any character for its pinyin and meaning
Every glyph on it is one the app teaches

screen.alt: A Chinese restaurant menu of noodles, rice, dishes, soup and drinks with prices and pinyin

features.title: See what's sticking
features.text: A calendar of every day studied, and each skill's progress on its own.
details: You'll recognise 学 long before you can write it, and it shows
What reviewing kept: still solid a month later
Rest days keep a streak standing

screen.alt: The Record: 140 characters, a 16-day streak, a calendar of study days and skill bars for recognise, pronounce, recall and write

features.title: Practice that's fair
features.text: No drill ever shows a character you haven't met yet.
details: Timed Sprint sheets, marked only when you hand them in
Handwriting allows slips and never sets reading back
A placement quiz credits only what you got right

screens.alt: Hanzi Quest's Today page: today's session, a five-step practice list, word of the week and flashcard decks
screens.caption: Today: a short list you can finish
